increments.title: Increment branches stay local; the issue branch carries the run state to the remote
increments.goal: The loop works every increment on a branch that never leaves the checkout, lands accepted work on the issue branch and pushes that branch after each landed increment, asks nobody for a remote branch deletion, and still resumes a dead run from the state on the remote.
criteria: No agent working an increment pushes its increment branch: every step of an increment commits locally and pushes nothing.
The planner pushes the issue branch to the remote after each increment it lands, so the remote holds every accepted increment up to that point.

No agent page and no workflow prompt asks for a remote branch deletion: the `git push origin --delete` instruction is gone from workflows/agile-loop.js and from agents/planner.md, and no other page asks for one.
The run state a resume reads reaches the remote with the issue branch, and the resume path no longer depends on an increment branch existing on the remote.
A resumed run works the increments still open and does not redo an increment the run state records as closed.
The reviewer still receives the increment's diff range and can read that diff with the increment branch present only locally.
An increment the review does not accept stays unmerged as it does today, its commits stay local and reach no remote, and the note the planner closes with still names its branch.
The run opens one pull request, for the issue branch, as it does today.

GOAL: increment branches never leave the checkout; the issue branch carries every accepted increment and the run state to the remote; nobody is asked to delete a remote branch.

BLOCKER CHECK THE ISSUE DEMANDS (settled: not a blocker). The agents of an increment share one git directory, so a local branch is visible to all of them and nothing has to be pushed for them to see each other's commits. Evidence: (a) workflows/agile-loop.js is a workflow script that the runtime hands only `args`, `agent`, `log` and `phase` (its header comment, lines 30-56) — it has no filesystem, and every role reaches the work through `agent()`, i.e. a subagent of the one session, in that session's checkout; (b) no prompt anywhere in the script orders a `git pull`, and the only `git fetch` calls are the three at lines 719, 846 and 1354 — yet every role reads `<issueDir>/backlog.json` out of the working tree with the helper right after the previous step committed it, which is only sound in a shared checkout; (c) branchBlock's continue text tells the next agent to `check it out`, an operation on the session's own tree; (d) the reviewer judges `git diff <issueBranch>...HEAD`, i.e. the HEAD of that same tree. So the pushes are not load-bearing and the issue is built, not raised.

NOTE ON THE CODEMAP: the run state carries none (`codemap` printed nothing, and the index says `hasCodemap: false`), so the map in `moduleMap` is mine. The planner's third decompose ruling was right that agents/reviewer.md and README.md need no change — reviewer.md says nothing about pushing or fetching, and the README's PUB node is the issue branch already. Two files it left out do need changing: skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md (the shared brief orders every agent to push every step's commit, which contradicts criterion 1) and test-repo.sh (the suite that asserts the current push behaviour).

THE CHANGE, FILE BY FILE.

1) workflows/agile-loop.js — `branchBlock` (lines 833-849). Create form: keep the two things that put the resume point on the remote — recording the branch name with the helper's `branch` subcommand while still on the issue branch, and committing and pushing THAT change on the issue branch — and keep `git checkout -b <incrementBranch>`. Drop `push it with \`-u\``. Add, once and here only, the prohibition that the rest of the increment inherits: the increment branch stays in this checkout and is never pushed. Write it as a priced prohibition that quotes the rationalisation it counters (.claude/rules/authoring.md, failure class 'a rule skipped under pressure'), because the shared brief's own price ('an unpushed commit dies with the container') is exactly the excuse an agent will reach for: name the price — this environment's proxy refuses `git push origin --delete`, so a pushed increment branch can never be removed, and the increment's commits are disposable until the planner lands them. Continue form: replace `git fetch origin <incrementBranch>` and the 'if the remote does not have it, create it from <issueBranch> and push it with -u' fallback with a purely local instruction — check the branch out in this checkout, and create it from the issue branch if the checkout does not have it. No remote is named in either form except the issue branch's push.

2) workflows/agile-loop.js — `recordStep` (lines ~587-604). The line 'Commit it with your work and push the commit.' is emitted into every step's prompt, increment steps included, so it has to vary. Give the function a fourth parameter for whether this step pushes, defaulting to the pushing form, and emit the push clause only for it; the other form stops at the commit and says nothing more about pushing, because branchBlock already carries the prohibition and the brief says state each thing once. Call sites: pass the non-pushing form from the four increment dispatches (research ~1127, tests ~1168, implement ~1192, review ~1284) exactly when `incrementBranch` is non-empty, and the pushing form everywhere else. The predicate is `incrementBranch !== ''`, not `issueBranch !== ''`: when the run has no branch machinery at all (`issueBranch === ''`, the state loader named no branch) the increments are worked on the checkout's own branch and every step must go on pushing, or the run state never reaches a remote at all. `decompose` and `replan:<id>` always take the pushing form — the planner works the issue branch.

3) workflows/agile-loop.js — the state loader prompt (lines 700-733). Delete the whole trailing-copy paragraph, lines 717-724 ('The checkout's copy of the state can trail ... keep the checkout's copy.'): it exists only because an in-flight increment's state used to reach the remote on the increment branch, and after this change no increment branch is ever on a remote. Put one sentence in its place saying the run state reaches the remote only with the issue branch, so the checkout's copy is the whole of it and no fetch is needed. The closing line that forbids anything beyond the read-only git commands named in the prompt then leaves exactly one: `git branch --show-current`.

4) workflows/agile-loop.js — the replan prompt (lines 1351-1362). Accepted form: drop `git fetch origin <incrementBranch>` (the branch is local) and delete the whole delete sentence at 1356-1358, including its 'A failed delete is a line in your summary' softener. Keep 'check out <issueBranch>, merge <incrementBranch>, push <issueBranch>', and state why the push matters — the remote then holds every accepted increment and the run state a resume reads. The second push (of the close itself) already comes from recordStep's pushing form; do not state it twice. Not-accepted form: keep it as it is — do not merge, check out the issue branch first, name the unmerged branch in the note — and add that the branch's commits stay in this checkout and that it is not pushed.

5) workflows/agile-loop.js — comments that would go stale. Line 815-818 ('so the abandoned branch keeps its name on the remote') — the abandoned name lives in the state and the checkout now. Lines 827-832 (branchBlock's header) — say that the first dispatch pushes the issue branch, not the increment branch, and why. Lines 737-741 — add that increment branches never leave the checkout. Line 1470-1471 ('Every agent above commits and pushes its own step') — only the steps on the issue branch push.

6) workflows/agile-loop.js — the publish prompt (1478-1528) is unchanged. It already pushes `<issueBranch>` and opens one pull request; criterion 8 is 'as it does today'.

7) agents/planner.md, lines 108-113. Accepted bullet: keep 'merge the branch into the issue branch and push', give the push its reason (the remote then holds every increment landed so far, which is what a resumed run reads), and delete the clause 'once your close is committed and pushed, delete that merged branch from the remote — one issue, one pull request'. Not-accepted bullet: 'the branch stays on the remote' is now false — it stays in the checkout, unmerged and unpushed, and the note still names it.

8) skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md, the 'Commit your step, then push it' rule (lines 18-28). Today it is an unconditional 'push that commit straight away' plus 'Never keep a commit local while you carry on working', which flatly contradicts the increment prompts. Re-cut it on an observable predicate, per .claude/rules/authoring.md ('behaviour that depends on a condition' — a rule keyed to an observable predicate, both branches stated, never an exemption bolted onto the general rule). The predicate is what the prompt names: where the prompt asks for a push, push straight away, with the existing price and the existing quoted excuses; where the prompt names a branch that stays in the checkout, commit to it and push nothing, with its own price and its own quoted excuse (the pull to push 'just in case' is the one to quote). Constraints on the edit: keep the exact strings the repository suite already greps for — 'push the commit' anywhere in the page, the quoted excuse '"one push at the end will do"', the sentence fragment 'an unpushed commit dies with the container', 'Never push to the default branch' and its quoted excuse '"the work is done and the branch is green"' (test-repo.sh lines ~413, ~3125-3148). Two other places in the same page state the push and need the same predicate, once each and no more: the branch sentence at line 54 ('every commit and push of your step belongs to that branch') and the closing 'Record your step, commit it with your work, and push the commit.' at line 202. The record recipe's command chain at line 188 ends in `&& git push`; the template is what an agent copies, so it needs the predicate visible at it — one short clause is enough, and the implementer decides whether it rides in the chain or in the sentence under it.

9) test-repo.sh — see the test plan. Two of its existing cases assert the behaviour this increment removes and must be re-cut rather than left to fail.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE. (a) Branches already on the remote from earlier runs are not cleaned up (the issue's non-goal). (b) Increment branches are still cut (non-goal). (c) A container that dies mid-increment loses that increment's local commits and the steps recorded on the increment branch; the run resumes from the last landed increment and works the open one again from the start, on a fresh `-take<n>` branch, because `incrementHasHistory` is false when no step of it is in the state the remote holds. That is exactly what criterion 4 asks for and no code change is needed for it. (d) One pre-existing hazard is left alone and is worth a follow-up issue: if a container dies mid-increment and the SAME checkout is resumed while still on the increment branch, the state loader returns that branch from `git branch --show-current` and the run treats it as the issue branch (which is why the publish prompt at line 1483 already apologises for it). It is out of this increment's criteria and unchanged in kind by this change.
